This image is Voronoi diagram。In mathematics, a Voronoi diagram is a spatial partitioning of a region into regions of equal measure. It is a popular example of a geometric algorithm. It is named after the French mathematician Pierre-Simon Laplace, who described it in 1807.
A Voronoi diagram is a partition of a region into a number of equal-sized regions, each of which is bounded by a curve called the Voronoi curve. The curve is a boundary of the region and is unique to each region. The regions are defined by a set of points called Voronoi points. The Voronoi points are the closest points to the boundary of the region. The Voronoi curve is the curve that connects the Voronoi points.
A Voronoi diagram can be used to partition a region into equal-sized regions. This is useful in a variety of applications, including computer graphics, image processing, and computer-aided design.
The Voronoi diagram can also be used to find the nearest point to a given point. This is useful in a variety of applications, including computer graphics, image processing, and computer-aided design.
